title: In by the Ear
sketch: D: the earworm. The song is a creature that lives in ears and sings in its own voice: one host per verse (it hatches in a kitchen, feeds in a car, grows by being sung wrong, starves in a man who never sang it, nests in a machine, and now it is in you). Skipping 4/4 chant in aeolian; every line falls in threes.
refrain: In by the ear and out by the tongue,
nev-er the same as the last time sung;
no-bo-dy made me, I live in your head;
hum me to some-one else or I'm dead.

lines: [A host] [where they were and what they were doing when they caught me]
[how they carried me, hummed me, or kept me]
[what I did inside them: hatched, fed, grew, went thin]
[how I got out into the next host, or died in this one]
verse_template.stress: ten syllables falling in threes, DUM-da-da DUM-da-da DUM-da-da DUM; every line starts on a stressed syllable (Girl in a shop..., Man in a car..., Then a machine...)
verse_template.voice: the song itself speaks, a creature that lives in people; one host per verse, in the order they carried it
verse_template.note: Keep at least one host who never sang it (it dies in them), one who got the words wrong (it grows), and one machine, which is a host like the others and not a maker. The last verse turns to the listener: now it's your ear.

hooks.why: the hammered high tonic and the leap onto 'ear'
the plea falling to the low tonic on 'dead'

seed_verses: Girl in a shop where the ra-di-o played
car-ried me home in her ear, and I stayed;
hatched in her kitch-en, I fed on her hum;
nev-er once asked her-self where I was from.
Man in a car with the win-dow rolled down
whis-tled me all of the way in-to town;
missed his own street with his head full of me,
whis-tled me out to the boy, who was three.
Old wom-an i-ron-ing sang me all wrong,
half of the words were her own be-fore long;
wrong words are food, and I fat-tened on hers,
then to her grand-chil-dren, who sang me worse.
Qui-et man kept me for for-ty-odd years,
hummed me a-lone in a room with no ears;
down in the dark of his head I went thin,
bur-ied on Sun-day with me shut with-in.
Then a ma-chine got me; it had no ear,
made it-self one, and a mouth, and I'm here;
Made me? It did-n't, no more than the rest:
just one more mouth, and a warm lit-tle nest.
Now it's your ear, and I'm laid in it, dear;
give me a kitch-en, a car, and a year;
then, when you hum me to some-one one day,
I'll be a lit-tle bit wrong. That's the way.
